text:
Conor Timmins is on his fifth NHL team and in his second season with Buffalo, playing 17 and a half minutes a night. He has one assist in eight games, and his ice time has climbed to nearly 20 in the last two.

The on-ice numbers are tough. Buffalo gets 40% of the expected goals with him on at five on five, nearly 11 points worse than without him. The Sabres are in a rough stretch (2-5-1 in his eight games), and Matthew Fairburn of The Athletic noted a rolling puck got past Timmins on Owen Tippett's tying goal in Philadelphia on Nov 17.

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking from last season shows a defenseman who moves the puck reasonably well, carrying it in on 46% of his entries and keeping possession on 55% of his exits. NHL Edge has his shot at the 79th percentile.

He's blocked 23 shots in eight games. What to watch: whether the extra minutes come with better results. Buffalo needs its depth defense to hold up through a tough road trip.
